v(g).advice: Your code has too many decision branches. Break large functions into smaller ones — each doing exactly one thing. Target complexity under 10 per function.

ev(g).advice: High essential complexity means unstructured control flow. Refactor nested conditionals into early returns.
steps: Replace nested ifs with guard clauses

v.advice: High volume means dense logic. Use Python built-ins, list comprehensions, and simplify expressions.

e.advice: High mental effort required. Add clear docstrings, rename variables, and reduce nesting.

b.advice: Halstead predicts likely bugs. Write unit tests and reduce complexity.

d.advice: Code is hard to write correctly. Simplify patterns and reduce unique operator variety.

loc.advice: Large files are harder to maintain. Split into modules by responsibility.

branchcount.advice: Too many branches make code hard to test. Consolidate or use lookup structures.

v_density.advice: High complexity relative to size. Spread complexity across more lines.

ev_ratio.advice: High ratio means unstructured complexity. Restructure control flow.

locode.advice: The code has many logical lines. Consider breaking into smaller functions.

l.advice: The program length is high. Simplify expressions and reduce nesting.

response_complexity.advice: Response complexity metric is elevated. Review function call patterns.

i.advice: Code intelligence metric indicates dense logic. Add documentation.

n.advice: Large vocabulary size suggests many unique operators. Consolidate patterns.

cyclomatic_loc.advice: High complexity relative to size. Spread complexity across more lines.

halstead_length.advice: High Halstead length indicates verbose code. Use built-ins and simplify.

halstead_volume_density.advice: Information is packed too densely. Spread it out for readability.

comment_quality.advice: Low comment coverage. Add explanations for complex sections.

uniq_op_density.advice: Many unique operators per line. Simplify and standardize.

branch_density.advice: Many branch points relative to size. Consolidate conditionals.
